case_title: Awadhesh Kumar v. State of U.P. & Anr.
aggravating_circumstances: Firing from close range, no provocation from victim, no weapon on victim's side
high_court_outcome: Converted conviction to s.304 Part I IPC
neutral_facts: The incident occurred when the accused, along with others, were involved in a quarrel with the victim. The accused fired at the victim from a close range with a country-made firearm, resulting in the victim's death. The victim and others did not have any weapon. The accused had previously been convicted, and during the altercation, the accused made a statement indicating no fear. The prosecution argued that the firing from close range indicated intent to cause death, and the trial court convicted the accused under Section 302 IPC. The High Court initially converted the conviction to Section 304 Part I IPC, but the Supreme Court restored the conviction under Section 302 IPC, finding that the case did not fall under Exception 4 to Section 300 IPC.
